findings.title: Run lock taken after the resume and fresh-run paths have already begun work
findings.description: `_locked` takes the lock inside the same call that starts the coroutine. A plain `--resume` or fresh run therefore holds the lock only for `asyncio.run`. Any pre-run checks in `run()` happen outside the lock. In `_locked`, `run_coroutine.close()` on a failed lock correctly avoids an unawaited-coroutine warning. The coroutine is built before the lock is attempted, though, so argument evaluation already ran. I did not confirm whether anything with side effects runs in that window.

findings.title: `_Stop` and `resume_item` control flow depends on an unreachable `raise AssertionError`
findings.description: The trailing `raise AssertionError("unreachable")` after the `with ExitStack()` block is dead code. It exists to satisfy the type checker because every branch inside the `with` returns. Restructure so the checker is satisfied without a dead statement.

findings.title: Unconstrained `item_rerun.replace` lookup can raise a bare `StopIteration`
findings.description: `next(i for i, r in enumerate(records) if r.index == record.index)` has no default. If the item index is not in the report, `StopIteration` escapes. In a coroutine this becomes a `RuntimeError`, which `resume_item` does not catch. `_check_record` validates the index earlier, so this is reachable only on a logic error. The same unguarded `next(...)` appears in `_reconcile` and `_outcome`. Pass an explicit default and raise a descriptive error.

findings.title: Line length exceeds the project's 88-character standard
findings.description: The signature `async def _write_each_report(report: BatchReport, runs_dir: Path | None, *, final: bool = True) -> None:` is over 88 characters. Several other new lines look longer than 88 too, for example in `item_resume.py#_check_record` and the new test files. I ran the awk length check and `ruff check`, but the output did not come back, so I cannot say which lines fail. The `UP`, `BLE` and `E` rules should catch this, so run `ruff check` and `ruff format` before merging.

findings.title: Private-function imports and a circular-import workaround
findings.description: `handle_item_resume` imports `_apply_param_overrides` and `_run_pipeline_sdk` from `run.py` inside the function, suppressing `reportPrivateUsage`. `run.py` imports this module, so the cycle is real. Passing these two callables in from `run.py` would remove both the cycle and the private-import suppressions.

findings.title: Executor's `each` step accumulates responsibilities
findings.description: `_execute_each_step` now handles normal batches, item reruns, halt recording, per-item report writes, flag-kind classification and dependency flags. The file is well past the ~300-line guideline. Consider extracting the report-lifecycle and flag-classification logic into a separate module.

findings.title: Atomic report write is sound, with one gap
findings.description: The temp-file-then-replace approach is sound, and OSError is logged with `logger.exception` and re-raised, as the rules require. A temp file can be left behind if `replace` fails, because `delete=False` is used and there is no cleanup. This is minor.

findings.title: Test coverage is strong
findings.description: The change adds tests for the lock, item resume validation, git preconditions, source reconciliation, report round-trips and flag kinds. Failure modes such as a held lock, unreadable report and failed write each assert an observable log or exit code. There is no load-test tier, but the changed paths are not simulation or network paths.
